# AI-Augmented Systems Analysis for Developers

> A practical, 7-module intensive course designed to help Software Engineers evolve into Product Engineers by mastering systems analysis, architecture design, and AI-driven documentation.

## Overview
This repository provides a comprehensive guide for developers (Backend/Frontend) who want to learn how to extract business requirements, design system boundaries, and write executable Product Requirements Documents (PRDs) without spending months on basic database or programming concepts.

The course heavily emphasizes using AI agents as architectural co-pilots and QA auditors.

## Target Audience
* Software Engineers (Middle/Senior)
* Tech Leads
* Developers looking to improve their system design and requirements engineering skills.

## Tech Stack Context
While the principles are universal, examples in the course are grounded in:
* Python (FastAPI/Django)
* PostgreSQL
* TypeScript (React/Vue)
* Docs-as-Code (Markdown, Mermaid, PlantUML)

## Course Modules (Located in `/guides`)
1. **System Boundaries & Architectural Context:** Problem framing (5 Whys), Stakeholder analysis, NFRs, C4 Model, DDD Bounded Contexts.
2. **Requirements Elicitation & Business Processes:** The Mom Test, BPMN 2.0 (AS-IS / TO-BE).
3. **User Scenarios & Backlog:** User Story Mapping, RICE prioritization, Use Cases (with a strong focus on Exception Flows).
4. **System Design (Data & Integrations):** ERD, Sequence Diagrams, OpenAPI/Swagger.
5. **Distributed Systems & Async Architecture:** Event-Driven Architecture, AsyncAPI, Saga Pattern, Transactional Outbox.
6. **Spec Anatomy (PRD Structure):** Modern PRD templates, Unit Economics, Feasibility Analysis, RBAC.
7. **Quality, BDD & Change Management:** Requirements quality criteria, BDD (Gherkin syntax), Traceability Matrix.

## How to Use
Users are encouraged to clone the repository, read the modules sequentially, and use the provided AI Prompts within each module to practice role-playing (e.g., interviewing a stakeholder) or validating their architecture with an LLM.

## Language
The course content is written in Russian.
